ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points D and E are respectively the midpoints of AB and AC. If the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 16, what is the area of quadrilateral BCED?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, points D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC, respectively,\\
then $DE \parallel BC$ and $DE= \frac{1}{2}BC$,\\
thus $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$,\\
since $\frac{DE}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
it follows that $\frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\frac{1}{4}$,\\
given that $S_{\triangle ABC}=16$,\\
then $S_{\triangle ADE}=\frac{1}{4}S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{4}\times 16=4$,\\
therefore the area of quadrilateral $BCED= S_{\triangle ABC}-S_{\triangle ADE}=16-4=\boxed{12}$.
